transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I’ve been having these really strange beliefs and experiences that feel completely real to me, and it’s starting to scare me. My mind feels like it’s going too fast and my mood is all over the place, and I just don’t feel like myself anymore, so I thought I should get help.

How long have these strange beliefs, fast thoughts, and mood changes been going on without a break, and were you feeling completely back to your usual self before this started or have you had similar episodes in the past?

They’ve been going on pretty much continuously for about a year and seven months now, without really going back to normal in between. Before this started I felt like my usual self, and I haven’t had anything like this happen to me in the past.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that other people don’t seem to notice, or feel that people are watching, plotting against, or trying to control you in some way?

Yeah, I hear voices pretty often, like people talking about me or giving me comments, even when no one is there, and sometimes I see shadows or figures that other people don’t react to. I also feel like cameras and strangers are watching me and that some group is tracking me or trying to manipulate what happens around me.

During this past year and seven months, have there been any weeks when your mood felt mostly normal or only mildly changed but the voices and paranoid feelings still continued just as strongly, or do the voices and paranoid thoughts only happen when your mood is very high, very low, or very unstable?

Yeah, there have definitely been stretches, like a couple of weeks at a time, where my mood felt more or less normal or just a bit off, but the voices and the feeling of being watched and tracked were still there just as strong. For most of this time my mood has been really high and revved up at the same time as the psychotic stuff, but the voices and paranoia haven’t gone away even when my mood calmed down.

During this whole period, have you also had clear episodes of feeling very down or depressed for at least two weeks at a time—like losing interest in things, feeling hopeless, or slowed down—or has your mood problem mainly been feeling high, revved up, or unstable rather than clearly depressed?

I’m not really sure I’ve had long stretches of feeling clearly depressed like that. It’s been mostly feeling really high, over‑energized, and all over the place, rather than slowed down or hopeless for weeks at a time.

When your mood is really high and over‑energized, do you end up doing things that are clearly out of character or cause serious problems—like spending lots of money, getting into risky sexual situations, using drugs more, or getting into trouble at work or with the law—or is it mainly just feeling revved up inside without major consequences?

When I’m in that really high, over‑energized state, I definitely do things that are out of character and it causes problems. I take on way too many projects at work and stay up late trying to do everything, get very flirty and more sexually driven than usual, and I’m a lot more impulsive socially, which has led to some conflicts and stress.

Thinking about this whole year and seven months, has there ever been a period of at least two weeks when your mood was clearly in a normal range (not high, not depressed) but the voices and paranoid beliefs were still present the whole time, or have your mood and the psychotic experiences always shifted together without that kind of clear break?

Yes, there was a period like that. For at least a couple of weeks my mood felt basically normal—not especially high or low—but I was still hearing the voices and having the paranoid thoughts just as much as before.

Over this past year and seven months, have you noticed a strong decline in your ability to function day to day—like withdrawing from people, losing motivation, or having trouble with basic self‑care and work or school—even when your mood isn’t especially high or unstable?

Yeah, it’s gotten a lot worse over that whole time. I’ve pulled back from friends and family, let chores and basic stuff like showering and cleaning pile up, and I struggle to keep up with work even when my mood isn’t super high or all over the place.

Have you been using any substances like cannabis, stimulants (such as cocaine or amphetamines), hallucinogens, or heavy alcohol during this time, and if so did your strange beliefs and voices start or clearly worsen around the times you were using them?

I drink a bit socially, but not heavily, and I don’t really use drugs like weed, coke, or hallucinogens. The strange beliefs and voices didn’t start around any substance use and don’t seem to change much based on whether I’ve been drinking or not.

Thinking about this whole year and seven months, would you say that you’ve spent most of the time feeling clearly manic or very over‑energized, or have there also been long stretches of months where your mood was mostly neutral or only mildly changed while the voices and paranoia continued?

Most of this time I’ve felt clearly manic or very over‑energized, with only shorter stretches where my mood was closer to neutral. Even during those more neutral periods, the voices and paranoia kept going, but the majority of the year and seven months I’ve been in that revved‑up, high state.

inference_history.note: Previously the only candidate was an unspecified primary psychotic disorder. Now we have more information: the patient reports over a year and a half of continuous psychotic symptoms (voices commenting, visual misperceptions, persecutory ideas of being watched and tracked), with no prior episodes and a clear change from previous baseline. This is consistent with a primary psychotic disorder of at least 12 months’ duration. However, they also describe their mind as going "too fast" and their mood as "all over the place," which raises the possibility of prominent mood symptoms. Because we do not yet know whether these mood symptoms meet full criteria for a manic episode, how long they last, or their temporal relationship to the psychotic symptoms, we must broaden the differential. A schizophrenia-spectrum disorder with continuous psychosis and possible mood symptoms remains likely, so a specific chronic primary psychotic disorder is included. But schizoaffective-type and mood-psychotic presentations must be considered until we clarify whether mood episodes are present for a substantial portion of the illness duration and whether there are periods of psychosis without mood disturbance. Therefore the candidates now include a primary chronic psychotic disorder, a psychotic disorder with both mood and schizophrenia-like features, and a severe mood episode with psychotic features. Further questioning about the nature, duration, and timing of mood symptoms, functional decline, and other features is needed, so the list has expanded and is not yet final.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had continuous psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, visual misperceptions, and paranoid delusions) for over one year, with clear functional decline, not attributable to substances. For most of this period there has been a prominent manic‑like syndrome (sustained elevated/over‑energized mood, increased activity, impulsivity, risky and out‑of‑character behavior) meeting criteria for a manic episode. However, psychotic symptoms have also been present for at least two weeks in the context of a clearly normal mood, indicating that psychosis is not exclusively mood‑congruent or confined to mood episodes. The overall course is dominated by manic symptoms, but with independent psychotic periods, fitting schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0) rather than pure schizophrenia or bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
